S50U26.five_day_thesis: Over the past 5 sessions the S50U26 future rallied +26.6 points (1070.0→1096.6, +2.5%) while max pain drifted up only once (1050→1060 on day one) and then held flat for 4 straight sessions, widening the spot-to-pain gap from 20 to 36.6 points. Put OI grew +48.3% (16,386→24,303) versus call OI's +9.6% (11,257→12,339), pushing the put/call OI ratio from 1.46 to 1.97 - a steady, accelerating hedge build, not short covering. The 1080 call wall held its strike across all 5 sessions (OI cycling 1,841-2,010) even as spot cleared it entirely, and the cumulative gamma-flip point has migrated up with spot to sit almost exactly at today's 1096.6 anchor. ATM IV compressed from 14.40% to a 12.98% mid-week low before ticking back to 13.72% alongside today's put-volume surge (+36.5% day-over-day). With real, persistent futures gains on 4 of the last 5 sessions and IV/volume confirming rather than fading the move, the 1060 max-pain anchor should be read as a weak tendency, not a target, in this cash-settled, 70-DTE series.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1050P / 1000P
strategies.rationale: The Protection-zone regime (P/C OI 1.97, put OI +48.3% over 5 sessions) argues for cheap defined-risk downside insurance rather than fading the rally outright.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid = ~6.0 points (1050 put last 11.0 - 1000 put last 5.0), i.e., ~1,200 baht per spread at the 200-baht multiplier.
strategies.invalidation: A sustained close above 1120 without a pullback would argue the put buying was defensive positioning against further upside, not a hedge that pays off soon - the spread would likely expire near worthless.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1100C / 1120C
strategies.rationale: Spot sits almost exactly at the cumulative gamma flip (1100) with call OI diffusing across 1090-1120 (1,182 / 1,409 / 568) rather than one dominant wall - a small, defined-risk fade of further near-term upside.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = wing width (20) - net credit (9.4, from 1100 call last 25.1 minus 1120 call last 15.7) = 10.6 points, i.e., ~2,120 baht per spread.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close above 1110 (next OI cluster, 1,242 call OI) breaks the fade thesis - the wall isn't holding.

strategies.name: Call debit spread 1110C / 1140C
strategies.rationale: 4 of the last 5 sessions closed higher (+26.6 points net) with put OI building defensively rather than distribution - a break through 1110-1120 with volume would validate continuation toward the 1140 strike.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid = ~11.8 points (1110 call last 20.3 - 1140 call last 8.5), i.e., ~2,360 baht per spread.
strategies.invalidation: A close back below 1080 (the former call wall, now support) invalidates the continuation thesis.

S50U26.prediction: Given the diffuse call OI cluster at 1090-1120 (1,182 / 1,409 / 1,242) and dealers turning long-gamma just above spot, expect near-term chop or soft resistance in the 1100-1120 band rather than a clean breakout, with the 1060 max-pain anchor acting as only a weak downside magnet if momentum stalls. This bias fails if S50U26 closes above 1120 on rising volume - that would confirm the put-hedge buildup is defensive positioning against a breakout rather than a topping signal, opening room toward the 1140 call strike. A close back below 1080 (the former call wall, now support) would instead argue the rally is exhausted and put the 1060 max-pain level back in play.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice; nothing here is an instruction to open or close a position. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the max-pain/wall dynamics described here are a tendency, not a guarantee, and are structurally weaker than for share-settled single-stock options; 70 days to expiry further dilutes any pinning effect. Defined-risk structures still carry their full stated max loss - size accordingly.
